title: Part 43: Aircraft Maintenance
description: Maintenance requirements, inspections, preventive maintenance, and airworthiness essentials

cards.back:
Required: Every 12 calendar months

Who performs: A&P with IA or repair station

Applies to: All aircraft (except those on progressive inspection)

Required when:
• Carrying passengers for hire
• Flight instruction for hire

Who performs: Any A&P or repair station

May exceed by 10 hours to reach inspection facility (counts against next interval)

Same scope of inspection!

Differences:
• Annual: 12 calendar months, requires IA
• 100-hour: 100 tach hours, any A&P

100-hour does NOT substitute for annual
Annual CAN reset 100-hour clock

Certificated pilots may perform preventive maintenance on aircraft they OWN or OPERATE

Limited to items in Part 43 Appendix A

Must make maintenance record entry

• Replenishing hydraulic fluid
• Replacing/servicing landing gear tires
• Replacing safety wire/cotter pins
• Servicing landing gear struts (adding air/oil)
• Replacing bulbs/reflectors/lenses
• Cleaning/replacing fuel/oil filters
• Replacing batteries
• Lubricating per manufacturer

• Replacing brake pads/linings
• Replacing spark plugs
• Adjusting control cables
• Replacing fuel lines
• Any engine work beyond oil change
• Propeller repairs
• Structural repairs

Must include:
1. Description of work performed
2. Date of completion
3. Signature of person performing work
4. Certificate number
5. Certificate type (A&P, IA, etc.)

For preventive maintenance: Pilot signs with certificate number

Legally enforceable FAA rule

Issued when: Unsafe condition exists and likely exists in other products of same design

Compliance: Mandatory-owner/operator responsible

Types: Emergency, immediately adopted, standard

Owner/Operator is responsible for:
• Knowing applicable ADs
• Ensuring compliance
• Maintaining AD compliance records

Check: FAA AD database before flight/purchase

Repair that might appreciably affect:
• Weight and balance
• Structural strength
• Performance
• Powerplant operation
• Flight characteristics
• Other airworthiness qualities

Requires: Form 337, IA approval

Alteration not listed in specs that might appreciably affect:
• Weight and balance
• Structural strength
• Performance
• Powerplant operation
• Flight characteristics

Requires: Form 337, IA or repair station approval

Major Repair and Alteration form

Required for:
• Major repairs
• Major alterations

Copies:
• One to FAA
• One stays with aircraft records

Approval that aircraft is airworthy after maintenance

Who may approve:
• Annual: IA or repair station only
• 100-hour: Any A&P or repair station
• Preventive maintenance: Person who did work
• Major repair/alteration: IA or repair station

Aircraft is airworthy when:
1. Conforms to type certificate (or approved alterations)
2. In condition for safe operation

Both conditions must be met!

Must be on board for flight:

A - Airworthiness certificate
R - Registration certificate
R - Radio station license (international only)
O - Operating limitations (POH/AFM)
W - Weight and balance data

Required: Every 24 calendar months

Who performs: Certified repair station or manufacturer

Must be done before operating in airspace requiring transponder

Required: Every 24 calendar months for IFR operations

Includes: Altimeter, encoding altimeter, static system

Who performs: Certified repair station or manufacturer

Inspection: Every 12 calendar months

Battery replacement when:
• 50% of useful life expires
• After 1 hour cumulative use

New expiration date must be marked on outside

Required: Every 30 days for IFR flight

Methods:
• VOT: ±4°
• Ground checkpoint: ±4°
• Airborne checkpoint: ±6°
• Dual VOR check: ±4° between receivers

Log: Date, place, bearing error, signature

Keep until:
• Work is repeated or superseded, OR
• 1 year after work performed

Permanent records (keep with aircraft):
• Total time in service
• Current status of inspections
• Current status of ADs
• Major alterations/repairs

Alternative to annual/100-hour

Benefits:
• Spreads inspection over time
• Good for high-utilization aircraft

Requirements:
• FAA-approved program
• Complete cycle = annual equivalent
• Detailed schedule required

Allows flight of aircraft not meeting airworthiness requirements

Purposes:
• Flying to repair facility
• Delivering/exporting
• Production flight testing
• Evacuating from danger

Issued by: FSDO or DAR

Per 91.403, owner/operator responsible for:
• Maintaining airworthy condition
• AD compliance
• Making aircraft available for inspection

May not operate unless maintained per Part 43

A&P = Airframe and Powerplant

May perform:
• Maintenance
• Preventive maintenance
• 100-hour inspections

May NOT perform:
• Annual inspections (needs IA)
• Major repairs without supervision

Additional authorization for A&P mechanics

May perform:
• Annual inspections
• Approve major repairs/alterations
• Approve return to service after annual

Requires: Experience, testing, renewal every 2 years

Without MEL, per 91.213(d):

1. Is it required by type certificate?
2. Is it required by 91.205?
3. Is it required by AD?
4. Is it required by other Part 91 rule?

If NO to all: Placard inoperative, deactivate or remove

FAA-approved document for specific aircraft

Allows operation with certain equipment inoperative

More flexible than 91.213(d)

Common for: Commercial operators, complex aircraft

FAA document containing:
• Aircraft specifications
• Operating limitations
• Required equipment
• Weight and balance data
• Approved modifications

Aircraft must conform to TCDS to be airworthy

Approval for modification to type-certificated aircraft

Examples:
• Engine upgrade
• Avionics installation
• Performance modifications

Becomes part of aircraft's approved configuration

PIC is responsible for determining aircraft is airworthy before flight

Includes:
• Preflight inspection
• Checking maintenance records
• Verifying required inspections current
• Checking for applicable ADs

Don't fly if in doubt!
